external_entities.name: colleagues
external_entities.description: People who sign in through the identity broker, including people using their own devices at home.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Colleagues sign in to it from wherever they are, including their own devices at home.

external_entities.name: franchise colleagues
external_entities.description: Colleagues from franchise stores who authenticate through their own identity provider.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Franchise colleagues do not have staff accounts with us; their own identity provider vouches for them and the broker takes that as a sign-in.

external_entities.name: HR system
external_entities.description: System that supplies colleague group membership changes to the identity broker overnight.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Group membership is not maintained there by hand — it comes from the HR system overnight.

external_entities.name: identity provider
external_entities.description: The identity provider used by franchise colleagues to vouch for them to the broker.
external_entities.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them

processes.name: identity broker
processes.description: Signs colleagues in, issues tokens, signs tokens, supplies public signing material, receives directory updates, and writes sign-ins to an audit log.
processes.source_excerpt: Everything colleagues use signs them in through one identity broker.

processes.name: store admin console
processes.description: Application that uses token groups to authorize changing prices and voiding transactions across every store.
processes.source_excerpt: The store admin console is one of those applications.

data_stores.name: key store
data_stores.description: Store holding the signing key used by the identity broker to sign tokens for every application.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker signs tokens with a signing key it keeps in a key store.

data_stores.name: directory
data_stores.description: The identity broker's directory of colleagues and their group memberships.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker keeps the colleagues and the groups they are in its own directory.

data_stores.name: audit log
data_stores.description: Log to which the broker writes sign-ins.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker writes sign-ins to an audit log.
data_stores.notes: Nobody has written down what that log records or whether it covers the franchise route.

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: Colleagues submit a sign-in to the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Colleagues sign in to it from wherever they are, including their own devices at home.
data_flows.notes: The source does not state the sign-in protocol or whether a second factor is used.

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: Franchise colleagues sign in through the broker using a vouch from their own identity provider.
data_flows.source_excerpt: We also let the franchise stores in.
data_flows.notes: The franchise authentication route is described, but its protocol and the permitted colleague population are not documented.

data_flows.name: vouch for colleagues
data_flows.description: The external identity provider vouches for franchise colleagues to the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them

data_flows.name: issue token
data_flows.description: The identity broker issues a token carrying a staff id and group list to colleagues.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Once the broker has signed a colleague in it issues them a token.
data_flows.notes: The token carries the colleague's staff id and a list of the groups they are in.
data_flows.data_description: token containing staff id and group list

data_flows.name: issue token
data_flows.description: The identity broker issues a token to authenticated franchise colleagues.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the broker takes that as a sign-in

data_flows.name: present token
data_flows.description: Colleagues present the broker-issued token to the store admin console.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every application takes that token and decides what the colleague may do from the groups in it.
data_flows.data_description: signed token with staff id and group list

data_flows.name: present token
data_flows.description: Franchise colleagues present the broker-issued token to the store admin console.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every application takes that token and decides what the colleague may do from the groups in it.

data_flows.name: fetch public half
data_flows.description: The store admin console fetches the public half of the broker's signing key to check token signatures.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Applications fetch the public half from the broker to check the signature.

data_flows.name: update membership
data_flows.description: The identity broker pulls HR changes into its directory overnight.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker pulls the changes once a night

data_flows.name: write sign-ins
data_flows.description: The identity broker writes sign-in events to the audit log.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker writes sign-ins to an audit log.

data_flows.name: use signing key
data_flows.description: The identity broker uses the signing key held in the key store to sign tokens.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker signs tokens with a signing key it keeps in a key store.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The network on which the identity broker and store admin console run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The broker runs on the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: home devices
trust_boundaries.description: Colleagues' own devices at home, outside the corporate network.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: including their own devices at home

trust_boundaries.name: franchise environment
trust_boundaries.description: The environment containing franchise colleagues and their own identity provider.

trust_boundaries.name: unspecified location
trust_boundaries.description: The location of the HR system is not stated.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: it comes from the HR system overnight

assumptions.assumption: The key store, directory, and audit log are in the corporate network because the broker keeps or uses them there.
assumptions.basis: The broker runs on the corporate network and is described as keeping or using these stores, but their locations are not stated.

assumptions.assumption: The directory is in the corporate network because the broker keeps it as its own directory.
assumptions.basis: The broker runs on the corporate network and keeps the directory as its own.

assumptions.assumption: The audit log is in the corporate network because the broker writes to it and its location is not otherwise stated.
assumptions.basis: The broker runs on the corporate network and writes sign-ins to the audit log.

assumptions.assumption: The key store is confidential because it contains the broker's signing key.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the key store holds a signing key.

assumptions.assumption: The directory is confidential because it contains colleagues and their group memberships.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the directory contains colleagues and the groups they are in.
